Template starts agents on a host from the templates that host lists in
its own <data dir>/templates.json: each names an agent and what it runs
(backend, model, directory, and a brief: the file it is asked to read
first). A host starts only what its file lists, so other hosts can start
its agents without being able to choose what runs there.

A request names a template and who asks, nothing else: no command,
directory, brief or model. The agent is named after its template, and is a
helper of whoever started it (name@host for an agent on another host, so
its replies go back there; none for a person). A template whose agent is
already there isn't started again: template resume brings back one that
has ended.

list, start and resume take --host to ask another host through the bus
(its bus serves template unless --remote-ops leaves it out). add and remove
edit this host's file only: no bus op writes it.

Usage:
  agent template [flags]
  agent template [command]

Examples:
  agent template list --host hub
  agent template start builder --host hub
  agent template resume builder --host hub
  agent template add builder --backend claude --cwd /srv/project --brief docs/lanes/builder.md
  agent template remove builder

Available Commands:
  list        List the templates a host agrees to start
  start       Start a template's agent on a host
  resume      Bring back a template's agent that has ended
  add         Add a template to this host's templates.json
  remove      Remove a template from this host's templates.json

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for template

Global Flags:
      --backend string          Backend for spawn or adopt: claude, aider, agy, or shell (spawn requires it or --backend-config; adopt auto-detects)
      --backend-config string   JSON file defining a custom backend (or app settings); pass it again to status/wait/watch for agents spawned with it
  -q, --quiet                   Don't print hints (results and errors still print)
      --termd-ns string         g3d-termd namespace (default: agents; never default or wall)

Use "agent template [command] --help" for more information about a command.
